results.title: H100 price per hour in 2026: GPU rental prices by chip
highlights:
The median advertised on-demand price of an H100 GPU-hour was $3.93 in the week of 9 Nov 2026, across 44 providers — up 31% on the same week a year earlier ($2.99). The B200 moved +47% over the same year, to $8.10.

| GPU | Latest week | A year earlier | Change | Providers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A100 | $1.91 | $1.70 | +13% | 38 |
| H100 | $3.93 | $2.99 | +31% | 44 |
| H200 | $5.11 | $3.50 | +46% | 34 |
| B200 | $8.10 | $5.50 | +47% | 23 |

Median of each provider's median advertised on-demand price. Chips with fewer providers move more from week to week.

## Two prices for the same hour

Published rate cards tell a different story from marketplaces. Our price board — built from the on-demand prices cloud providers publish — put the on-demand H100 hour at $4.11 on 13 Nov 2026, against a marketplace median of $3.93 in the week of 9 Nov 2026.

Neither number is “the” price. List prices show what providers ask for capacity on demand; marketplace medians show where spare capacity clears; reserved and contract prices, usually lower again, sit in agreements that are rarely published in full. For anyone valuing a neocloud, lending against GPUs or underwriting a datacentre lease, the spread between the three says how tight capacity is.

## What moves the price of a GPU-hour

- Supply of the newest chips. When a generation is scarce, its hourly price holds up and pulls older chips with it.
- Power and space. A GPU earns only once it sits in a powered, cooled hall; grid connections and building timelines now set the pace more than chip deliveries.
- Contract mix. Providers that sold most of their capacity on multi-year take-or-pay contracts have less to offer on demand, which supports on-demand prices.
- Economic life. The price an owner needs depends on how many years a GPU can earn before it is replaced — see GPU-hour economics.

...

What does an H100 cost per hour in 2026?

The median advertised on-demand price was $3.93 per GPU-hour in the week of 9 Nov 2026, across 44 providers. Reserved and contract prices are usually lower.

How much does a B200 cost per hour?

The median advertised on-demand price of a B200 GPU-hour was $8.10 in the week of 9 Nov 2026, across 23 providers.

Are GPU rental prices falling?

Not for the H100 over the past year: its median on-demand price is up 31% on the same week a year earlier. Scarce new chips, power-limited capacity and long take-or-pay contracts have kept on-demand prices up.

results.title: NVIDIA H100 Price in 2026: Buy, Build or Rent
results.author: Artem Bukhkalov
highlights:
Renting is the other way in, and it is the market we measure. At the Compute Census index of 6 Nov 2026, the median on-demand price of an H100 80GB is $3.90 per GPU-hour, the cheapest accepted offer is $1.30 and the most expensive list price is $12.29. A published 12-month reserved rate stands at $3.26.

$3.90 H100 median, on-demand, per GPU-hour index of 6 Nov 2026

$1.30 floor cheapest accepted on-demand offer

$12.29 ceiling 9.5× the floor

$3.26 12-month reserved−16% vs median

...

| Provider | Offer | USD / GPU-hr | As of |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lium.io | Marketplace | $1.30 | 2026-09-21 |
| Beam | On-demand | $1.83 | 2026-10-20 |
| CoreWeave | Spot | $2.46 | 2026-10-20 |
| Runpod | On-demand | $2.69 | 2026-10-16 |
| Civo | Reserved, 12 mo | $2.69 | 2026-10-20 |
| Civo | On-demand | $2.99 | 2026-10-20 |
| DigitalOcean | Reserved, 12 mo | $3.26 | 2026-09-28 |
| Runpod | On-demand | $3.99 | 2026-10-16 |
| Lambda | On-demand | $3.99–$4.29 | 2026-10-16 |
| DigitalOcean | On-demand | $4.41 | 2026-10-20 |
| Nebius | On-demand | $4.50 | 2026-10-16 |
| CoreWeave | On-demand | $6.16 | 2026-10-20 |
| AWS | On-demand | ~$6.88 | 2026-10-16 |
| Google Cloud | On-demand | ~$11.00 | 2026-10-16 |
| Microsoft Azure | On-demand | $12.29 | 2026-10-16 |

...

Against 1 Oct 2025, the H100 median has moved +100%. The longer history explains the turn. Through 2024 and 2025, rental prices fell as new capacity came online and Blackwell systems began shipping. AWS cut on-demand prices for its P5 H100 instances by 44 percent from 1 June 2025, with savings plans cut by up to 45 percent. Many observers read that as the start of a long slide.

The slide stopped. SemiAnalysis reported in April 2026 that on-demand capacity was sold out and that H100 contracts were being renewed at the same rates signed two to three years earlier, some for four years through 2028. Its one-year H100 contract index rose from $1.70 per GPU-hour in October 2025 to $2.35 by March 2026. Providers then raised list prices: Nebius lifted its on-demand H100 rate to $4.50 per GPU-hour from 1 October 2026, about 17 percent higher, its second increase in three months according to Silicon UK. AWS now lists Capacity Blocks for its eight-GPU H100 instance at $47.757 per instance-hour, or $5.970 per GPU-hour.

SemiAnalysis attributes the turn to demand that outran the arrival of new capacity: on-demand pools sold out, and older GPUs that were expected to cheapen stayed booked on long contracts. Our own index records the same turn in the median, which is why the history above is worth more than any single quote.

...

The index records several kinds of offer, and they are not interchangeable. On-demand capacity can be started and stopped by the hour. Reserved capacity is committed for six months to three years in exchange for a lower rate, and the published 12-month rate sits −16% against the on-demand median at this snapshot. Spot and preemptible capacity is cheaper again, but the provider can take it back. Serverless offers bill by the second for inference. Our floor and median leave spot and preemptible offers out, so a cheap interruptible rate never pulls the headline down.

...

results.title: GPU rental prices in 2026: H100, H200 and B200 per hour
results.author: Safeguard Security Team
highlights:
In October 2026, published on-demand list prices for an H100 ranged from about $2 to about $12 per GPU-hour, depending on the provider, the billing model and what is bundled. Specialist clouds mostly sit between $3 and $6. Spot and long commitments can cut the price by half or more. B200 list prices run from about $6 to $14.

...

- AWS Capacity Blocks, p5.48xlarge (8 H100s), N. Virginia, Ohio and Oregon: $47.757 per instance-hour, $5.970 per GPU-hour. AWS Capacity Blocks pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- AWS p5.48xlarge on-demand (8 H100s), N. Virginia, Ohio, Oregon: $6.88 per GPU-hour, as checked by IntuitionLabs on 10 October 2026.
- Azure NC40ads H100 v5 (1 GPU), East US, Linux pay-as-you-go: $6.98 per hour. Azure ND96isr H100 v5 (8 GPUs): $98.32 per VM-hour, $12.29 per GPU-hour. Azure Retail Prices API, 19 October 2026.
- Google Cloud a3-highgpu-8g (8 H100s), Iowa, on-demand: $88.49 per VM-hour, which is $11.06 per GPU-hour. IntuitionLabs, 10 October 2026.
- Oracle Cloud BM.GPU.H100.8: $10.00 per GPU-hour list. IntuitionLabs, 10 October 2026.
- CoreWeave HGX H100, 8 GPUs, on-demand: $49.24 per instance-hour, about $6.16 per GPU. CoreWeave pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- Lambda H100 SXM, 8-GPU instance: $3.99 per GPU-hour. Lambda pricing page, 19 October 2026. IntuitionLabs records $2.99 in a 2025 snapshot.
- Runpod H100 SXM: $3.99 Secure Cloud and $2.69 Community Cloud. H100 PCIe: $1.99 Community Cloud. Runpod pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- Nebius HGX H100 on demand: $4.50 per GPU-hour. Nebius prices page, 19 October 2026. IntuitionLabs says this took effect on 1 October 2026, up from $3.85.
- H200 on-demand list prices: $5.29 (Runpod Secure Cloud), $5.40 (Nebius), about $6.31 (CoreWeave, $50.44 per 8-GPU instance). Provider pages, 19 October 2026.
- B200 on-demand list prices: $6.69 (Lambda, 8 GPUs), $7.99 (Runpod Secure Cloud), $8.50 (Nebius), $8.60 (CoreWeave, $68.80 per 8-GPU instance). AWS Capacity Blocks: $14.208. Provider pages, 19 October 2026.
- B200 index price: $2.31 per hour in early March 2026 and $4.95 in late April 2026, per the Ornn Compute Price Index as reported on tomtunguz.com on 27 April 2026.

...

A GPU-hour is one GPU rented for one hour.

...

- The chip variant. The H100 comes in a PCIe version and an SXM version. SXM is the faster, more tightly connected one used in 8-GPU servers. Runpod's own page lists its H100 PCIe and H100 SXM at different prices for this reason ($1.99 and $2.69 in Community Cloud).
- Whether the price is per GPU, per node or per cluster. CoreWeave quotes a whole 8-GPU instance, while Lambda and Nebius quote per GPU. The IntuitionLabs survey divided node prices by eight to compare and warns that node pricing distorts per-GPU comparisons.
- The billing model. On-demand means you pay by the hour with no commitment. Spot or preemptible means cheaper capacity that the provider can take back. Committed means you promise a term. Prepaid capacity blocks mean you reserve a window in advance.
- Region and operating system. AWS and Azure prices vary by region, and Azure's Windows rates are higher than Linux for the same VM ($8.82 against $6.98 for the NC40ads H100 v5 in East US, per the Azure Retail Prices API on 19 October 2026).
- Memory. AWS's P5 page lists 80 GB of HBM3 per H100 and 1,128 GB of HBM3e per 8-GPU H200 instance, about 141 GB per GPU. More memory lets a larger model or a longer context fit on fewer GPUs, which is part of why the H200 costs more.

The IntuitionLabs survey says plainly that its entries mix prepaid capacity, on-demand VMs, pods, and cluster and node rates, and are not interchangeable. Its inclusion rule is publicly displayed hourly rates for a matching product, taken from first-party pages, with promotional rates excluded. It is a survey by one publisher, not an official price index, and its method is as the publisher describes it.

...

The large clouds charge the most on-demand. IntuitionLabs lists AWS at $6.88 per GPU-hour for the 8-GPU instance in three US regions and $8.60 in N. California. Azure's own price feed shows $6.98 for a single-GPU VM and $98.32 for the 8-GPU VM in East US, which is $12.29 per GPU. IntuitionLabs lists Google at $11.06 per GPU in Iowa and Oracle at $10.00.

...

Lambda's 1-Click Cluster product lists H100 at $6.16 per GPU for 16

...

Several of these went up. According to the survey, AWS Capacity Blocks rose from $5.19 to $5.97, Runpod Secure Cloud H100 SXM from $3.29 to $3.99, Lambda's 8-GPU SXM from $2.99 (a 2025 snapshot) to $3.99, and Nebius's HGX H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 effective 1 October 2026. The current figures match the providers' own pages on 19 October 2026. The survey says AWS on-demand and Azure list prices were not re-verified as lower than the 2025 third-party figures.

...

First-party list prices on 19 October 2026 give a clearer picture than earlier in the year:

- H200 on-demand: Runpod Secure Cloud $5.29 and Community Cloud $3.59; Nebius $5.40; CoreWeave $50.44 per 8-GPU instance, about $6.31 per GPU.
- H200 Capacity Blocks on AWS: $6.866 per GPU-hour on p5e.48xlarge and $7.895 on p5en.48xlarge, in the US regions listed.
- B200 on-demand: Lambda $6.69 per GPU on an 8-GPU instance and $6.99 for one GPU; Runpod Secure Cloud $7.99 and Community Cloud $5.98; Nebius $8.50; CoreWeave $68.80 per 8-GPU instance, about $8.60 per GPU.
- B200 Capacity Blocks on AWS: $113.666 per instance-hour, $14.208 per GPU-hour, on p6-b200.48xlarge.
- B200 clusters on Lambda: $9.86 per GPU for 16 GPUs, $9.36 for 64 and $8.87 for 256 or more, for terms of two weeks to a year.

...

The index view is different. The Ornn Compute Price Index, reported in a post dated 27 April 2026 on tomtunguz.com, put the B200 at $4.95 per hour that week, up from $2.31 in early March, a 114% rise in six weeks. The author also reports that the B200 premium over H200 fell to $0.28 per hour in November 2025 and widened to $1.80 by late April 2026. That is one index, from one author, describing a spot style market, so its levels sit below most on-demand list prices. The takeaway is directional: Blackwell prices were rising in spring 2026, and the gap to the previous generation was widening.

...

Several forces act at once, and sources disagree about their weight.

Supply. When new chips ship in volume, older chips tend to fall in price. IntuitionLabs records that AWS announced an up to 45% price reduction on 5 June 2025, which the survey says included about 44% off H100 on-demand, and that providers cut H100 rates by roughly 20 to 25% in single moves in June and July 2025. That is the historical context for 2025.

Demand. The tomtunguz.com author argues that frontier model releases coincide with jumps in demand for the newest chips. The author links the B200 spread widening to a model launch in February 2026 and a larger context window in April 2026 that needs more memory. The author admits the correlation is not perfect and that supply shocks matter. This is an author's interpretation, not a measured fact.

Capacity running out. The October 2026 increases at Lambda, Nebius, Runpod and AWS Capacity Blocks suggest H100 capacity is tighter than in mid 2025. The survey reports the increases but does not give reasons, and none of the providers states a cause on its pricing page.

Contract structure. As the companion explainer on GPU as a service economics sets out, large providers sign multi-year take-or-pay contracts. Capacity already promised to big customers is not available to walk-up renters, so list prices can rise while some marketplace offers stay low.

results.title: NVIDIA B200 Price in 2026: Specs and GPU Pricing | fal
results.author: Jim Cai
highlights:
The NVIDIA B200 is the first-generation Blackwell data-center GPU: 192 GB HBM3e, 8 TB/s of memory bandwidth, NVLink 5 and native FP4. Few teams buy one outright, so the price that matters is the rental rate. B200 time is sold three ways: an hourly list rate, per-second billing on serverless platforms, and lower reserved or committed rates. On fal Serverless a B200 costs $7.99 per GPU-hour at list price, billed per second only while a runner is alive, and as low as $5.49 per GPU-hour with committed capacity.

- What is the smallest unit you can rent? Some offers only rent whole 8-GPU servers, so the real hourly price is eight times the per-GPU rate.
- What is the billing granularity? Hourly billing rounds up. A 10-minute test on an hourly plan costs a full hour.

results.title: Nebius quietly changed how it prices preemptible GPUs on October 8, a week after raising on-demand rates. | Devanshu Rajput
results.author: Devanshu Rajput
highlights:
Nebius quietly changed how it prices preemptible GPUs on October 8, a week after raising on-demand rates.

Preemptible H100, H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000 moved from fixed rates to dynamic spot pricing. The published number is now a floor, not a price.

For the H100, that means "$2.15 per GPU-hour" became "from $0.79." The B300 went from $4.30 to a floor of $0.99.

The mechanics matter more than the floor. Nebius says spot prices move with capacity, utilisation and demand, can change as often as every 15 minutes, and can change during use. The ceiling is one cent below the on-demand rate for the same capacity.

So on an H100 the possible range is now $0.79 to $4.49 an hour, on the same chip, in the same region, depending on when you run.

That's a different planning problem from a fixed preemptible rate. You can model a fixed rate in a budget. A range this wide needs you to watch the actual price, not the rate card.

Two things worth knowing: this is the second Nebius change this month, after the October 1 on-demand increase, and the H100 is in one region only, eu-north1.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Explained: On-Demand, Reserved, Bare Metal
highlights:
- On-demand buys flexibility: You pay per GPU-hour with no commitment and can stop at any time, which suits experiments, bursty jobs, and workloads whose utilization you have not measured yet.
- Reserved pricing buys a lower rate: Committing to a term lowers the effective hourly price, but you pay for every hour of the term, so it only saves money when utilization stays above the break-even point set by the discount.
- Bare metal is a deployment model, not a billing term: It gives you the whole physical server with root access and no hypervisor, which can be bought on demand or reserved, and NVIDIA has measured virtualized training running 12% slower than bare metal.
- Published rates are only a starting point: On GMI Cloud, on-demand rates start at $2.60 per GPU-hour for H100, $3.20 for H200, $5.00 for B200, and $8.00 for GB200 as of October 2026, while committed plans are discounted and storage and networking are priced separately.
- Utilization decides which model wins: Cast AI’s 2026 analysis of production clusters found average enterprise GPU utilization of roughly 5%, which shows how easily reserved capacity turns into paid idle time. Matching the pricing model to measured usage is the single biggest lever on GPU cost.

...
